messages:
ada: heads up — noticed a spike of tiny-gang evictions in ap-southeast1 around 06:05 UTC. a bunch of nodes went from Ready -> NotReady quickly
mike: saw that too. looks correlated with an autoscaler run. dumping scheduler events now
infra-bot: autoscaler: scaleDown candidates selected 10 -> 4 in ap-southeast1 at 06:03 UTC (policy: cost-trial).
yara: i pulled the logs: nodes annotated gpu-anchored=true were included in candidates. that shouldn't happen
dave: why did the predicate ignore gpu-anchored? we added that annotation to prevent tiny-gang preempts
mike: policy push earlier: cost-trial lowered unneededTime to 2m and scaleDownUtilizationThreshold to 0.25 (change-id: pol-2026-03-07-11) — infra-bot shows the rollout at 05:50 UTC
infra-bot: policy-push: cost-trial by dave@infra.
ada: (typo) yikes. can you roll back? these jobs checkpoint poorly
dave: rolling back now. reapplying unneededTime -> 10m and threshold -> 0.5
ops-bot: action created: AUTOSCALE-230 investigate policy experiment (assigned to dave).
yara: mitigation: i'll taint affected nodes no-scale-down=true:NoSchedule and annotate pods prevent-scale-down=true so we don't lose more progress
ad a: updated taints/annotations. watch for new evictions
mike: metrics: pod_evictions jumped 0 -> 26 in 3m, now dropping after taint and rollback :thumbsup:
dave: i'll add a guard to the rollout pipeline so policies lowering unneededTime below 5m require a canary cluster flag
yara: long-term: reintroduce an explicit cluster-autoscaler predicate honoring gpu-anchored and add integration tests with warmpool + tiny-gang
ad a: logging the affected job ids: 7801, 7802, recommend checkpoint restart once nodes stable
mike: recap for postmortem: cause = aggressive policy change for cost experiment -> autoscaler removed gpu-anchored nodes -> evictions; mitigation = rollback + taint/annotate; next = add rollout guard + predicate test + alert on evictions/sec for GPU pools
dave: noted. will follow up on AUTOSCALE-230 and AUTOSCALE-231 (rollout guard). thanks all.
